## Welcome

Hailing from the Netherlands, I have bounced between Europe and North America
in pursuit of one abiding question: how do people---politicians and citizens
alike---arrive at their political judgments and decisions? The search has
taken me to the intersection of political science and psychology, with
rigorous quantitative methods as my instruments of choice. Increasingly,
those methods draw on computational social science, and this blend of
political science, psychology, and computation now defines my work. I have
ranged across many topics, but my current interests center on theoretical and
methodological approaches to choice modeling, polarization in complex
ideological landscapes, AI and political cognition, and AI in social science
research methods. I am currently a professor of political methodology at the
University of Zurich. I am also the co-editor of
*Advances in Political Psychology*, as well as associate editor of various
other journals.

This site collects my [CV](cv.qmd), [teaching materials](teaching.qmd),
[software](software.qmd), and [working papers](papers.qmd). For occasional
longer-form writing, subscribe to my Substack,
[Augmented Inquiry](https://augmentedinquiry.substack.com).

## Interests

- Choice modeling
- Polarization in complex ideological landscapes

- AI in social science research methods
